note: Adjudicated accidental variants (punctuation). Substantive text agrees across all three witnesses with zero variants. The adopted reading is the approved Benziger printing's (Ordo Missae, p. 286): no stop after the third Sanctus, and the divine title unbroken. The two other editions punctuate the opening title differently — do closes the threefold acclamation without a stop and detaches Deus Sábaoth, handmissal-eo does the reverse.

adjudicated.ruling: No stop after the third Sanctus, with do and with the approved Benziger printing, which sets Sanctus Dóminus unbroken (Ordo Missae, p. 286): the third acclamation is not a member closing a list but the predicate of what follows — Sanctus Dóminus, 'holy (is) the Lord'. The hand missal's comma stands where its page prints a bell glyph and marks the ringing, not the syntax; its own chant page sets the phrase with no comma there.

No comma before the apposition Deus, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.confiteor w064: Dóminus Deus Sábaoth is one unbroken title. DO's comma follows the Vulgate's punctuation at Is 6:3 (Dominus, Deus exercituum), which the liturgical books do not carry over.

No comma before the relative, with handmissal-eo: qui venit is the subject of benedíctus, not a parenthesis — 'blessed (is) he who comes'. DO's comma is the Vulgate's at Mt 21:9 (benedictus, qui venit); the missal's own Ordo prints the phrase unbroken, and so does the hand missal's chant page.
